name: OR-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 6-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Incumbent Val Hoyle's fundraising and outside support advantage
Prediction markets price Hoyle near 94% to win
No public general-election polling, limiting precision
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Hoyle: a D+6 district, incumbency, a large fundraising edge, and outside spending on her side, with markets pricing her around 94%. With no polls available, the forecast stays close to fundamentals but trims slightly for uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late public polling or a surge of outside spending against Hoyle could narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Val Hoyle seeks a second term in a southwestern Oregon district that leans Democratic by about six points. She has out-raised Republican Monique DeSpain roughly two to one and holds a cash advantage, with outside groups also spending on her behalf. DeSpain has raised a modest sum for a challenger and lacks outside support so far. Prediction markets give Hoyle about a 94 percent chance of winning, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. The main caveat is the absence of public general-election polling, so the estimate rests on fundamentals rather than direct measurement. Even with that uncertainty, the combination of district lean, incumbency, and money makes Hoyle a clear favorite, though not immune to a late shift in the political environment.
